claim: While INSTALL_LOCK is unset the unauthenticated installer page echoes the configured database password and SMTP password into the HTML form fields
limitation: Install() fills the form from loaded settings (install.go:74,100), AssignForm puts it in ctx.Data (:113) and the template renders value={{.db_passwd}}. Image setup sets the lock only when SECRET_KEY is non-empty (setup:28-32). Severity is High here but section 2.2 says V-1 and V-2 are both Medium: Narrative inconsistency, not a source defect.

claim: Reverse-proxy authentication trusts the identity header without checking the request origin and can auto-register users
anchor: Verification of header data is not performed
limitation: Code comment says verification is left to the proxy; auto-register path at reverseproxy.go:64-68 depends on isAutoRegisterAllowed (a separate setting). Default off confirmed in ini:872 and service.go:175.

claim: When SECRET_KEY is empty the code falls back to a fixed constant shared by every installation
limitation: Constant fallback at security.go:151 (value omitted from this row's claim). Installer generates a key only if none (install.go:393-400). Secret key used for 2FA secret (twofactor.go:101-104) and migration credentials (task.go:73-88). Impact sentence about LDAP, Actions secrets and webhook headers rests on other files not cited in the row.

Correct the citation to security.go:167 and 209-212.

limitation: Empty token goes straight to promhttp; route registered only if Metrics.Enabled (default false).

limitation: Secret is assigned from the form unencrypted (setting/webhook.go:255) and used raw as HMAC key (deliver.go:91); header goes through EncryptSecret (webhook.go:224).

claim: The AES key for two-factor secrets is a single unsalted MD5 of the secret key
limitation: getEncryptionKey returns md5 of SecretKey used for AesEncrypt/AesDecrypt.

SameSite default is lax (session.go:38-40 default, :66-75 parse of SAME_SITE). Protection depends on the Go stdlib check (browser Sec-Fetch-Site/Origin headers); not tested at runtime.

claim: MFA: TOTP and WebAuthn with optional enforcement; not enforced by default
limitation: SignInPost redirects to /user/two_factor or /user/webauthn when the user is enrolled (auth.go:326-366); TWO_FACTOR_AUTH accepts only empty or enforced (security.go:193-199) and TwoFactorAuthEnforced defaults false (security.go:80). Enforcement is consulted by the web context and the API (context.go:202-206, api.go:226-240). Sources whose TwoFactorShouldSkip is true bypass local 2FA (auth.go:327-330), and Actions or deploy-key doers are exempt from enforcement (api.go:229); neither exception is stated in the Narrative cell. Enrolment and verification handlers were not read end to end.

claim: Cookie flags: HttpOnly, SameSite and derived Secure
limitation: Both the session cookie (session.go newCookie, written by store.go:133) and site cookies (cookie.go SetSiteCookie) set HttpOnly always, SameSite from SessionConfig and Secure from SessionConfig.Secure. Secure is derived, not forced: COOKIE_SECURE defaults to whether AppURL starts with https:// (setting/session.go:64), so a deployment with an http AppURL sends cookies without Secure. cookie.go:95-96 (a second helper) also sets the flags; not read in detail.

claim: Outbound request filtering: webhook and migration transports use an egress policy that blocks non-public targets in lax mode
limitation: Both transports are built from the egress policy with WithLocalNeedsIPAllow and a dial-time check (policy.go:242-244); default EGRESS_MODE is lax (security.go:29). The ini text (:539-562) states the list is enforced on direct connections only: with an HTTP proxy configured the target is resolved by the proxy and only the host name is checked (policies.go:90-97). Scope is webhooks and migrations; other outbound fetches were not audited. The dial-time implementation (policy.go dialContext) was read only in part.

claim: Build: make build builds the frontend and the backend; CI builds for several platforms on pull requests
limitation: Makefile:477 builds frontend and backend; the backend target depends on generate-backend and the gitea executable (Makefile:483). pull-compliance.yml:81-109 cross-compiles linux/arm64, windows/amd64 and linux/386 with go build (not make build) on pull_request (line 4), and the job runs only when backend or actions files changed (line 82); the frontend job runs make frontend. So CI proves cross-compilation, not make build itself.

claim: Test: make test-backend for unit tests, make test-integration against a chosen database, make test-migration and make test-e2e
limitation: test-backend runs go test over GO_TEST_PACKAGES, which excludes the integration, migration and modelmigration packages (Makefile:107). test-integration compiles the integration tests and runs tools/test-integration.sh; the database comes from GITEA_TEST_DATABASE, defaulting to sqlite only for local test goals (Makefile:30-33). The script, database setup and e2e shell script (tools/test-e2e.sh) were not read, and no test was run.

claim: Deploy: release binaries and container images are built by the nightly and tag workflows; standard image copies docker/root, rootless image copies docker/rootless; environment deployment is Unknown
limitation: Nightly runs on a 12-hour schedule or manual dispatch (release-nightly.yml:3-6); the tag workflow runs on pushed tags v[0-9]* excluding pre-release suffixes (release-tag-version.yml:3-8), so release candidates are not built by it. Both workflows build and publish artifacts (binaries to object storage or release, images to registries with push: true); neither deploys to a running environment, which matches the cell's own Unknown. Workflow steps were read, not executed.

claim: Upgrade: helper script stops the service, takes a dump, downloads the release, verifies checksum and signature, swaps the binary and starts the service; the application migrates the schema at start
limitation: Order and conditions were wrong in the Narrative: the script requires gitea to be running (line 14), downloads the binary and verifies the checksum first (99-108), verifies the GPG signature unless --ignore-gpg is given (109-115), and only then flushes queues, stops the service, dumps, swaps the binary (keeping a .bak) and starts it (123-136). Schema migration at start happens because AUTO_MIGRATION defaults to true (database.go:89, db.go:44-45); when disabled and the version differs the process exits fatally (db.go:53-56). Narrative cell corrected. The script was read, not run.

claim: Backup: gitea dump writes a zip of files and the database; the upgrade script passes extra options through backupopts
anchor: Description: `Dump compresses all related files and database into zip file.
limitation: Zip is the default format; dump.go:93 shows other output types exist, chosen by the file extension or a type flag. The upgrade script sets backupopts at line 32 and expands it into giteacmd dump at line 130. Which files the dump includes (skip flags, custom paths) and whether a dump restores cleanly were not checked; no scheduled backup was looked for beyond the scheduled jobs block.

claim: Secret rotation: gitea generate creates new internal tokens, JWT secrets and secret keys; the code states that rotating an existing secret key is not yet supported, so there is no supported rotation procedure for existing data
anchor: // Until it supports rotating an existing secret key, we shouldn't move users off of the widely used default value
limitation: generate has INTERNAL_TOKEN, JWT_SECRET (alias LFS_JWT_SECRET) and SECRET_KEY subcommands that only print a value (generate.go:54-77, 103-110). The FIXME comment (security.go:148-149) says rotation of an existing secret key is not yet supported; a grep of cmd, modules/secret, models/auth and models/webhook found no re-encryption or rotation command (the only rotation code is for login cookies, models/auth/auth_token.go). The row's cite cmd/generate.go:56-73 is short of the SECRET_KEY definition by four lines (it ends at 77); the claim still holds. Absence of a procedure rests on that search, not on the whole repository.

claim: Restore dependencies: make deps, from the repository root
anchor: deps: deps-frontend deps-backend deps-tools deps-py ## install dependencies
limitation: deps fans out to deps-frontend (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile via node_modules), deps-backend (go mod download), deps-tools (go run -exec true over seven tool packages, which compiles linters and generators and needs network) and deps-py (uv sync). Needs Go, pnpm and uv on the PATH first; the Narrative states that no single command installs them. Cite 555-556 covers only the deps line; the sub-targets are at 558-582. Not executed.

claim: Build: make build, from the repository root
limitation: Makefile:477 defines build as frontend plus backend; backend runs generate-go and then the $(EXECUTABLE) rule (Makefile:483, 501). The frontend target needs the node_modules from make deps-frontend, so make deps (or its frontend and backend parts) comes first. The cite Makefile:477-478 ends on a blank line and .PHONY: the defining line is 477. Not executed.

claim: Run: ./gitea web, from the repository root
limitation: The web subcommand starts the server (web.go:38-44). The binary is named gitea on non-Windows hosts (EXECUTABLE ?= gitea, Makefile:57) and appears in the repository root after make build; on Windows it is gitea.exe (Makefile:54). Without an existing configuration the installer is served (web.go:285-286). Not executed.

claim: Test: make test-backend, from the repository root
limitation: Runs go test over GO_TEST_PACKAGES, which excludes integration, migration and modelmigration packages (Makefile:107); it is the unit-test target only. Database-backed tests in the covered packages use the repository's test helpers; whether every package passes without extra services was not checked. Not executed.

claim: API returns 403 naming required scopes: the message lists the required and held scopes
anchor: ctx.APIError(http.StatusForbidden, fmt.Sprintf("token does not have at least one of required scope(s), required=%v, token scope=%v", requiredScopes, scope))
limitation: Required level is Write for POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE and Read otherwise (api.go:291-294), and the check is skipped when the doer has no token scope (api.go:285-288, e.g. password Basic auth). The Narrative cites 303-306; the whole check is 280-306. Route-to-category wiring (tokenRequiresScopes callers) was not traced.

claim: API returns 403 not available for public-only tokens: use a token without the public-only restriction
anchor: ctx.APIError(http.StatusForbidden, "this endpoint is not available for public-only tokens")
limitation: rejectPublicOnly returns 403 only when IsPublicOnlyDoer is true (api.go:251-255); the exact text is longer than the quoted symptom, which is a substring. Which routes attach rejectPublicOnly and how IsPublicOnlyDoer is derived from the token scope were not traced.

claim: Git client gets 401 Update your password: server answers git clients with the translated message auth.must_change_password, English text Update your password; browsers are redirected to the change-password page
limitation: The branch is taken when MustChangePassword is true for a non-bot, non-impersonated doer (auth.go:71) and the path is not the change-password page; a client counts as git when its User-Agent starts with git (web.go:200), not by protocol. The locale string is Update your password (json:383). Git HTTP routes use the same web verify middleware (optSignInFromAnyOrigin); the route-by-route wiring was not traced.

claim: Startup logs repeated ORM engine initialization attempt #n/m failed (message abbreviated: the real line ends with the error); the server retries and then stops
anchor: log.Error("ORM engine initialization attempt #%d/%d failed. Error: %v", i+1, setting.Database.DBConnectRetries, err)
limitation: The real line is 'ORM engine initialization attempt #%d/%d failed. Error: %v' (db.go:35), so the abbreviation note is accurate. Retries default to 10 with a 3 second backoff (database.go:87-88). After the last attempt InitDBEngine returns the error without a further failed line (db.go:32-34) and the startup caller turns it into a fatal log (init.go:68-75, 136); the install path returns it to the installer page instead (install.go:442, not read in detail). The Narrative cite db.go:29-41 does not itself contain the stop.

claim: Two-factor validation fails with maybe SECRET_KEY is wrong: the error text names the cause; an administrator can disable 2FA from the CLI
anchor: return false, fmt.Errorf("validateTOTP unable to decrypt (maybe SECRET_KEY is wrong): %w", err)
limitation: The message is returned when AES decryption of the stored secret fails; the key is an MD5 of SECRET_KEY (twofactor.go:101-104). The caller turns it into a server error (2fa.go:65-68), so the text appears in the server log and error page rather than as a normal invalid-code message. disable-2fa takes --username or --id and removes the user's TOTP and WebAuthn credentials via DisableTwoFactor (cmd/admin_user_disable_2fa.go:19-68). The cell's claim that users enrolled before a key change cannot be recovered is consistent with a one-way AES key but not otherwise tested.

claim: Installer page keeps appearing or startup logs 'Is Gitea already running?': listener failure is logged and a graceful shutdown starts; the installer is served while the lock is unset
anchor: log.Error("Unable to open listener for installer. Is Gitea already running?")
limitation: The log text appears only when the installer listener fails (web.go:152-156); the installer route set is served only while setting.InstallLock is false (web.go:285-286). Whether INSTALL_LOCK is read correctly from the configuration file was not traced.

claim: Startup stops with 'Can not find APP_DATA_PATH': process exits with a fatal log
limitation: os.Stat on AppDataPath fails, then log.Fatal (web.go:212-213). The check runs only after the installer branch, so it applies once the lock is set. The Narrative cites :213 only. Writability is not checked here; the cell's 'and is writable' check is operator advice, not code.

claim: Git hooks or gitea manager return 403 from the internal API: missing INTERNAL_TOKEN is logged and answered 403; a wrong token also answers 403
limitation: authInternal answers 403 when InternalToken is empty (internal.go:27-31, with a Warn naming the missing setting) and when the X-Gitea-Internal-Auth bearer value does not match by constant-time compare (internal.go:33-40). Callers (hooks, manager) were not traced; the token comparison is the whole check.

claim: Browser shows 'Failed to authenticate user' with 401: the handler logs the error and returns 401
limitation: AuthShared error leads to log.Error('Failed to verify user: %v') then 401 (web.go:160-165). Which auth methods can produce the error was not enumerated.

claim: API returns 401 'token is required': sign in or supply a token; a bad credential gives 'invalid username, password or token'
limitation: reqToken returns 401 'token is required' when the request is not signed in (api.go:311-318); apiAuth returns 401 with 'invalid username, password or token' unless the error carries its own user message (api.go:864-872). Route wiring of reqToken not traced.

claim: API returns 403 'This account is not activated.' or 'You must change your password. Change it at: ...': activate or change the password at the address in the message
anchor: ctx.JSON(http.StatusForbidden, map[string]string{"message": "This account is not activated."})
limitation: Both messages come from verifyAuthWithOptionsAPI for a signed-in doer (api.go:884-896), as a JSON message field. The same function also answers 403 for a prohibited login, which the row does not list. The password-change address is built from AppSubURL (api.go:893).

claim: Git over HTTP returns 403 'This repo is archived' or 'not allowed': handler sends a plain-text message
anchor: ctx.PlainText(http.StatusForbidden, "This repo is archived. You can view files and clone it, but cannot push or open issues/pull-requests.")
limitation: The archived message applies only to pushes (githttp.go:125 requires !isPull) and the 'not allowed' text is 'Interacting with repositories by HTTP protocol is not allowed', sent when DisableHTTPGit is true (githttp.go:41-45). Both are plain-text 403s.

claim: SSH push reports 'Repository is in a broken state' or 'Mirror Repository ... is read-only': serv returns the message from the internal API
limitation: IsBroken gives the broken-state 403 (serv.go:166-169); a mirror gives 'Mirror Repository %s is read-only' only when the requested mode is above read (serv.go:171-175), so the abbreviation note is accurate. PrivateUserErrorf returns the text as UserMsg in JSON (services/context/private.go:69-71). The SSH client display of the message was not traced.

claim: Startup exits because the database version differs from the expected one: run the migrate command or enable automatic migration
anchor: log.Fatal(`"database.AUTO_MIGRATION" is disabled, but current database version %d is not equal to the expected version %d.`+
limitation: migrateWithSetting migrates when AUTO_MIGRATION is true (default, database.go:89) or when the database is uninitialised; otherwise a version mismatch is fatal with the advice to set AUTO_MIGRATION or run gitea migrate (db.go:43-57). The migrate command itself was not read.

claim: Runner reports 'unregistered runner': interceptor refuses the request; re-register with a current registration token
limitation: withRunner returns the error for an unknown UUID or a token that fails verifyRunnerToken (interceptor.go:55-66); Register is exempt. Registration rejects an inactive token with 'has been invalidated, please use the latest one' (runner.go:57-59). The runner-side files named in the Checks cell are not in the Target.

claim: Package client receives 401 with a Basic realm: the registry adds the challenge header and refuses
limitation: reqPackageAccess sets the Basic realm and returns 401 on a token-scope mismatch (api.go:52-55) and on insufficient package access mode (api.go:59-62; the Narrative cite ends at 58 and misses this second branch). Other 401 sources in individual registries were not checked.

claim: Metrics scrape returns 401: an empty or wrong header is refused
limitation: With a token configured, a missing Authorization header or a mismatch (constant-time compare) gives 401 (metrics.go:21-31); with no token the endpoint is open (metrics.go:17-19, see V-7).

claim: Reverse-proxy authentication trusts the identity header without checking the request origin and can auto-register users
anchor: Verification of header data is not performed
limitation: Code comment says verification is left to the proxy; auto-register path at reverseproxy.go:64-68 depends on isAutoRegisterAllowed (a separate setting). Default off confirmed in ini:872 and service.go:175. Narrative cite list now includes reverseproxy.go:64-68 (the auto-register branch); 110-118 is the Verify entry that logs the user in.
